facts.text: The validation window is the period of less than four months after the prototype arrives in mid-2027 in which the Collision Mitigation System must be validated.
facts.quote: The validation window is the period of less than four months after the prototype arrives in mid-2027 in which the Collision Mitigation System must be validated.

facts.text: The manufacturer's last comparable function took three to four years to validate, mostly through physical testing and tuning on each machine model.
facts.quote: The last comparable function at this manufacturer took three to four years, mostly through physical testing and tuning on each machine model [Introduction].

facts.text: The new Collision Mitigation System validation target is under four months in the second half of 2027.
facts.quote: The new target is under four months, in the second half of 2027 [Chapter 2].

facts.text: No case was found in any industry of a new automatic braking function going from first representative hardware to accepted validation in about four months.
facts.quote: No case was found, in any industry, of a new automatic braking function going from first representative hardware to accepted validation in about four months

facts.text: Every documented reduction in physical testing rested on years of earlier investment, a narrow operating domain, or both.
facts.quote: every documented reduction in physical testing rested on years of earlier investment, a narrow operating domain, or both [Introduction, Chapters 1, 2, 13].

facts.text: The booklet concludes that the four-month validation window cannot be compressed, but most of the work can be moved before the prototype arrives: the scenario catalog, existing-fleet data pipeline, simulation and bench tools, and credibility evidence can all be prepared beforehand.
facts.quote: the four months cannot be compressed, but most of the work can be moved in front of them: the scenario catalog, the data pipeline on the existing fleet, the simulation and bench tools and the credibility evidence can all exist before the prototype arrives [Chapter 1].

facts.text: The validation window should follow a fixed sequence: correlate by measuring latency, detection range and stopping on the real prototype; multiply by rerunning correlated scenarios virtually; confirm with whole-machine tests of the worst cases; then use shadow mode, with live operation but braking disabled.
facts.quote: correlate (measure latency, detection range and stopping on the real prototype), multiply (re-run the correlated scenarios virtually), confirm (whole-machine tests of the worst cases), then shadow mode (live operation with braking disabled) [Chapter 1].

facts.text: The prototype's four-month window is intended for final validation, not for constructing validation capability.
facts.quote: It is a final validation window, not a capability-construction window [Chapter 2].

facts.text: The validation window in the second half of 2027 contains no northern winter.
The EU Machinery Regulation applies from 20 January 2027.
facts.quote: the EU Machinery Regulation applies from 20 January 2027

facts.text: If the Collision Mitigation System's perception uses machine learning, the lead time for a notified body alone could exceed the four-month validation window under the EU Machinery Regulation.
facts.quote: the EU Machinery Regulation applies from 20 January 2027, so if the perception uses machine learning, the lead time for a notified body alone could exceed the window [Chapter 1].

facts.text: The booklet's most repeated conclusion is that the validation window should be a confirmation and calibration campaign for a method already proven before the prototype arrives; the window constrains the whole plan.
facts.quote: The booklet's reframing, that it should be a confirmation and calibration campaign for a method already proven before the prototype arrives, is its most repeated conclusion [Introduction, Chapters 1, 6, 10, 13].
